comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted English Philosophy annual plan has ten required 6 EC first-year units, eight required and two selected 6 EC second-year units, and 30 EC of open study, two 6 EC philosophy choices, a 6 EC thesis seminar and a 12 EC thesis. The example selects Theoretical Philosophy and World Philosophies I in year two, and Contemporary Ethics and History of Philosophy in year three. The World Philosophies I/II condition is met once. Both first-year and second-year Philosophical Encounters seminars carry zero credits, as does the English language test. The test or completed refresher gates Academic English. The binding study recommendation requires 42 first-year EC and the language quality requirement. Political Philosophy includes a Broader Mind certificate. The thesis requires all first-year courses and 48 second-year EC, and is assessed by two readers. Open study has level, approval and non-overlap rules. The distinct Dutch Philosophy Plus routes do not enter this example.
components: The English language test or a completed refresher is required before the grade can be awarded.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized canonical name is Philosophy, the corrected registry attribute lists ENG, and the current adopted OER explicitly names Philosophy as its English track. The distinct Dutch Filosofie track has other variants and a different credit structure, so the exact named track is selected without regard to UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, argument and historical perspectives
alternatives.concept: Study philosophical arguments about mind, emotion, free will, politics and moral responsibility. Read historical and contemporary texts, and use rhetoric and close reading to examine how arguments are made and interpreted.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains direct philosophy courses and an argumentation strand, complemented by historical and intercultural sources.
progression: Introductory philosophy, political philosophy and rhetoric lead into ethics, mind, logic and philosophical arguments on freedom and emotion. Rhetoric in Action follows introductory rhetoric and uses mainly Dutch in work with local schoolchildren.

alternatives.label: Ethics, climate and public reasoning
alternatives.concept: Use ethics and political philosophy to ask who bears responsibility for climate harm and how governments, firms and individuals should respond. Use climate science, life-cycle assessment and environmental justice cases to evaluate those arguments.
alternatives.labelReason: Climate Change, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, Governance of Sustainability and related communication and economic courses ground the ethical questions in public decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Seven courses (52.5 EC) differ in each direction. Climate science, justice, communication, economics, life-cycle assessment, sustainability governance and environmental media distinguish the applied option from the rhetoric, heritage and literature work in the first option.
progression: Introductory philosophy and economics lead into ethics, climate justice and communication. Life-cycle assessment and political philosophy inform later work on governance and public arguments.

candidates.label: Practical philosophy of climate, markets and public decisions
candidates.assessment: Ethics and Political Philosophy include applied contemporary questions in the exact English track. Dutch PLUS governance rows are acknowledged as separate variant evidence, not used to assert an English formal governance route. UCR retains6 dedicated philosophy courses45 EC plus legal-philosophical and ethical-rhetorical work; seven climate/economic/governance courses provide a distinct application.

candidates.label: Theoretical philosophy of mind and knowledge
candidates.assessment: A separate theoretical option would reuse the five PHIL courses and logic already central to the closest option. Psychology/AI could add contexts but would change the disciplinary organising object; no distinct philosophical sequence is established.

candidates.label: Dutch-track PLUS philosophy with religion and theology
candidates.assessment: A genuine Dutch-track variant, outside the selected English comparator. No sustained UCR religion/theology sequence is established by myths, archaeological context or general philosophy. It is rejected, not implemented through adjacent subjects.

selection.assessment: Two defensible options use philosophy as the taught subject, including six dedicated philosophy courses in each, complemented by legal philosophy and logic. The second option offers a distinct application in climate ethics and public reasoning. A mind-and-knowledge direction would rely on the same philosophy courses and shift toward empirical psychology if extended. The Dutch religion and governance variants do not establish additional routes within the English comparator.

notes.text: VU devotes separate courses to global philosophical histories, epistemology and philosophy of science. It also requires close-reading seminars and an individual philosophy thesis. UCR develops philosophical arguments in ethics, mind, agency and political philosophy. Rhetoric in Action involves mainly Dutch interaction with local primary-school children. Independent research at UCR is optional and sits outside the displayed schedules.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Philosophy studies historical, practical and theoretical philosophy. Students learn to evaluate arguments, read demanding texts closely and write an individual philosophy thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One UCR option combines philosophy with rhetoric and historical interpretation. The other applies ethics and political philosophy to climate responsibility, markets and public decisions.

curriculum.limitation: The English-track example includes 30 EC of open study and a 12 EC individual thesis. Thesis entry requires all first-year courses and 48 EC from year two. The language test or refresher is required for the Academic English grade.
